chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Buzay', from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him: The people narrate that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast Ramadan for twenty-nine days more often than he fasted it for thirty.
He said: They lied. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) only fasted a complete month, and the obligatory duties are not incomplete.

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created the year as three hundred and sixty days, and created the heavens and the earth in six days, so He deducted them from three hundred and sixty. Thus the year is three hundred and fifty-four days.
And the month of Ramadan is thirty days, according to the word of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And to complete the period,' and the complete one is full.
And Shawwal is twenty-nine days, and Dhu al-Qadah is thirty days, according to the word of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And We appointed for Moses thirty nights.' So the month is thus.
And We appointed for Moses thirty nights
Then according to this, there is a complete month and an incomplete month, and the month of Ramadan never decreases, and Sha'ban never becomes complete.

key_terms.لِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ: And to complete the period (Quranic verse)

ai.seo_question: Why is Ramadan always 30 days and Sha'ban always 29 days according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the narration that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) frequently fasted Ramadan for twenty-nine days. He asserts that the obligatory fast is always complete (thirty days) because the divine obligations are never incomplete. The Imam explains the lunar calendar structure: a year of 354 days is composed of alternating 30-day and 29-day months, with Ramadan always being the 30-day month and Sha'ban always being the 29-day month, citing Quranic verses regarding the completion of periods and the nights appointed to Moses.
